Noah (Data): Quick question 11 I'm keeping my NYC apartment but moving a week-to-week setup in Raleigh starting June. Can I have the WFH stipend split across two homebases or do I have to pick one as my official homebase? Also worried if this creates any payroll/tax obligations for Redwood in NC.
Lina (People Ops): Good Q. We prefer one official "homebase" in Workday for payroll/benefits. You can still book a satellite hub and mark recurring remote days, but payroll needs a single state for withholding.
Noah (Data): So stipend split isn't supported? I was hoping to get 50/50 since I'll be 50% in each state.
Ben (Payroll): We do day-level proration for stipend when someone's homebase change happens mid-month, but we don't split a recurring monthly stipend across two states simultaneously. Payroll needs one tax/withholding state. If you spend >183 days in one state later in year that might be considered your tax residence.
Noah (Data): Ugh, OK. If I keep NY as homebase but work 50% from NC, could that still trigger employer registrations in NC?
Ben (Payroll): Potentially yes. Even if your official homebase is NY, an employee physically working in NC for regular weeks can require us to register for unemployment tax and payroll withholding in NC. For a single headcount it usually is limited to payroll registrations, but some states have stricter rules.
Marta (Benefits): Also flag: health carriers occasionally require a primary residence for network purposes. If you maintain a NY address but are predominantly in NC for care, you may need to update the carrier during open enrollment or earlier for continuity of care.
Noah (Data): What do you recommend I do before signing any lease or making the split regular?
Lina (People Ops): Two options: A) Pick a single official homebase now (e.g., NY) and treat Raleigh as temporary travel; we'll document scheduled remote days. B) If Raleigh will be long term, change your homebase and let payroll trigger withholding and benefits checks. Whichever you choose, submit the homebase change form or a remote schedule note.
Noah (Data): Can you escalate to Tax Counsel to check employer registration risk in NC? I don't want to surprise hiring ops or legal.
Ben (Payroll): Will do. I'll loop in Tax Counsel and share the registration guidance. Expect a reply in 48-72h.
Tax Bot: Automated note  Tax Counsel will review multi-state telework risk. Typical next steps: confirm expected days in NC, assess payroll unemployment registration, state withholding, and local taxes.
Lina (People Ops): Practical steps here: 
1) Pick tentative official homebase in Workday or submit homebase-change form if switching.
2) Share an estimated weekly schedule (e.g., Mon/Tue in NY, Wed-Fri in Raleigh).
3) Send lease copy / utility if you change homebase.
4) Payroll/Tax will confirm registration needs.
5) Benefits will confirm carrier network impacts.
Noah (Data): I'll keep NY as homebase for now and post my weekly schedule here by Friday. Thanks everyone :rocket:
Marta (Benefits): Noted  we'll check carriers once you post schedule.
Ben (Payroll): Looping: payroll@redwood.com in case docs need uploading.
Noah (Data): Posted schedule in thread — thanks again :+1:
